title: Saturday, 6:55 a.m.
intro: A flat full of cables and cat hair. Everything is labelled, in a very good hand.

items.label: Red ribbon on the doorknob
items.text: The red ribbon. A bow so neat you suspect it was tied by someone who has done it before. Many times. For many doors.

items.label: Mirror
items.text: A velvet face with a bow tie already knotted. Your fingertips are pruned. You will do the show in gloves, like a very sophisticated surgeon.

items.label: Static (deaf white cat)
items.text: Static can't hear a thing. She presses her entire body against the speaker cabinet anyway and goes completely still, whiskers pointed at the lake window.

items.label: Playlist sheet
items.text: A month of Dedication Hours, typed. Tonight: Fair Weather Friend, Always Be Near, I'll Be Seeing You, Rock of Ages, Waters of March. Next week: Another Day, Tomorrow, Evening Star, River Deep. Down the margin, in pencil, the first letters, circled.

items.label: Reel: NIGHT WATER, 1959
items.text: A tape box. On the label, a woman's neat hand: 'Low Mercy Chapel Choir. Hymn 212.' Cued on the machine. Vern has been looking at it for three weeks.

items.label: Calendar: LAST SHOW
items.text: Tonight's square is circled three times: 'LAST SHOW.' Underneath: 'close with the hymn?' A question mark, hit so hard it tore the page.

items.label: Microphone
items.text: A beautiful old ribbon mic. You say 'Good evening' to it in your best voice. It is a very good voice. It isn't yours.

items.label: Photograph: WMRC, 1961
items.text: A young man at a console, laughing at something off-camera. L. Page, on the back. Behind him the window is full of lake.

items.label: Fan letters
items.text: 'Dear Vern, play 'Moon River' for my husband's ghost.' 'Dear Vern, can you stop saying 'goodbye' on the radio.' (You never do.)

items.label: 45s, alphabetised
items.text: The only archive in town sorted properly. Even the typos are in order.

items.label: Kettle
items.text: Warm. Someone put it on. You pour a cup. You drink it. It tastes of kindness and a faint hint of lake.

items.label: Plant
items.text: A cactus named Sir Richard Branson. It is alive out of spite.
